draft.title: Science and pseudoscience
card: Science tests claims against evidence. Others can repeat the tests, and the claim is changed or dropped if the evidence does not support it.
Pseudoscience uses science-sounding words and looks scientific, but it avoids fair tests. It does not change its claims when evidence goes against them.
Pseudoscience often relies on stories, such as "it worked for my cousin", and on claims that cannot be tested at all. A story about one person is not a fair test.
Ask two questions of any claim: Can it be tested? What happens to the claim when a test goes against it?
draft.remember: Science follows the evidence. Pseudoscience avoids tests and does not change.

a.q: Which feature best shows that a claim is science rather than pseudoscience?
opts: It is tested, and changed if the evidence disagrees
It uses technical words and scientific-looking terms
It is supported by many personal stories of success
It has been believed by many people for a long time
a.why: Science tests claims and changes them when the evidence does not fit. Technical words can be copied by pseudoscience, so they do not show that a claim has been tested.
a.clue: Think about what is done with the claim when a test goes against it.

b.q: A company says its "energy bracelet" improves balance. It shows the buyer's glowing reviews, uses terms such as "quantum frequency", and says any failed test was "unfair". Why is this pseudoscience?
opts: It relies on stories and rejects tests that go against it
It is sold by a company that wants to make money
It has not yet been tested by any other scientists
It uses words that most people do not understand
b.why: The claim rests on reviews and dismisses tests that do not support it, so it will not change when evidence goes against it. Science-sounding words do not make it scientific, and a profit motive alone does not make a claim pseudoscience.
b.clue: Look at what the company does when a test goes against its claim.

a.best: It is tested, and changed if the evidence disagrees

b.best: It relies on stories and rejects tests that go against it
